name: Ireland
seoTitle: History of Ireland: The Emerald Isle, Green-White-Orange Tricolor, and 1916 Easter Rising
metaDescription: Discover the detailed history of Ireland. Explore Celtic heritage, the 1916 Easter Rising, Michael Collins, the 1921 Anglo-Irish Treaty, and the Tricolor flag.
mapFormation:
Occupying roughly five-sixths of the island of Ireland in the North Atlantic across 70,273 square kilometers, the Republic of Ireland (Éire) is celebrated as the 'Emerald Isle' due to its lush rolling green pastures nourished by mild Atlantic Gulf Stream rains.

Gaelic Celtic culture, law (Brehon Law), and Ogham script flourished for over a millennium prior to the arrival of Saint Patrick in the 5th century CE, who established Christian monastic centers that preserved classical European literature through the Dark Ages ('Isle of Saints and Scholars').

Following the Anglo-Norman invasion of 1169 and centuries of English and British rule, the partition of the island was codified under the Government of Ireland Act 1920 and the Anglo-Irish Treaty of 1921, creating the self-governing Irish Free State (26 southern counties) while Northern Ireland (6 counties) remained in the UK. Full sovereign republican status was formally enacted with the Republic of Ireland Act 1948.
flagHistory:
The national flag of Ireland—the Bratach na hÉireann (The Irish Tricolor)—features three equal vertical bands of green, white, and orange, first flown on March 7, 1848, by revolutionary nationalist Thomas Francis Meagher in Waterford.

The tricolor is a sublime vexillological symbol of peace and reconciliation between traditions: Green represents the Roman Catholic and Gaelic majority; Orange represents the Protestant minority (honoring King William III of Orange); and the central White band symbolizes a lasting truce and fraternal unity between the two traditions.
freedomStory:
Ireland's struggle for independence culminated in the heroic events of the early 20th century.

On Easter Monday, April 24, 1916, Patrick Pearse, James Connolly, and the Irish Volunteers seized the General Post Office (GPO) in Dublin, reading the Proclamation of the Irish Republic (the Easter Rising). Although military victory was suppressed, the execution of the leaders ignited mass national support.

In the 1918 election, Sinn Féin MPs convened the first revolutionary parliament (Dáil Éireann) at the Mansion House in Dublin on January 21, 1919. Following the Irish War of Independence led by Michael Collins, the 1921 Anglo-Irish Treaty established the Irish Free State. In 1937, the people ratified Bunreacht na hÉireann (the Constitution of Ireland). Today, Ireland is a prosperous European tech and pharmaceutical hub (the 'Celtic Tiger').
challenges: As a member of the European Union, Ireland navigates post-Brexit arrangements preserving the 1998 Good Friday Peace Agreement and an open, frictionless border with Northern Ireland. Domestically, major priorities include resolving urban housing supply shortages across Dublin and Cork, expanding offshore Atlantic wind energy, and preserving the Irish language (Gaeilge).

faqs.question: What is the meaning of the colors on the Irish flag?
faqs.answer: Green represents the Catholic and Gaelic tradition, Orange represents the Protestant tradition (King William of Orange), and White represents lasting peace between them.

faqs.question: How do you distinguish Ireland from the UK in Google Street View?
faqs.answer: In Ireland, both front and rear plates are white (in the UK, rear plates are yellow), speed limits are in km/h on yellow diamond signs, road edges have dashed yellow lines, and all directional signs are bilingual in Irish (Gaeilge) and English.

timeline.event: Saint Patrick arrives in Ireland, spreading Christianity and monastic learning.
The Anglo-Norman invasion initiates centuries of English administration.
The Great Famine (An Gorta Mór) devastates the population, prompting mass global emigration.
The Easter Rising in Dublin proclaims the Irish Republic on April 24.
The Anglo-Irish Treaty establishes the self-governing Irish Free State.
The Good Friday Agreement establishes a historic peace settlement for Northern Ireland.
